text.en: Đúng rồi! That means 'correct' — and you are!
Tuyệt! (That's 'awesome,' by the way.) 😎
YES. You heard it. I saw your ears work.
Giỏi quá! So clever.
Nailed it. Don't even act surprised.
Ooh, smooth. Do it again, I liked that.
Correct! Okay you're kind of good at this.
That's the one! *leaf-sprouts wiggle*
Perfect. We make a great team, huh?
Yep yep yep! Keep that energy.
Chuẩn! ('Spot on.') Look at you go.
Easy for you now, apparently. Proud!
Không sao! ('No worries.') Here's the one we wanted:
Ooh, so close. That tone is genuinely sneaky. Look:
Honestly? That one got me too. The answer's:
Cố lên! ('Keep going!') Not quite — it's actually:
Almost! Tiny miss. The word we needed:
Nope — but a GOOD nope, you were close. It's:
Hmm, not this time. Let's see the right one together:
That meant something else (sneaky language). Here you go:
No biggie — even my leaves get confused. Correct one:
Eh, language is tricky. Here's the fix:
Okay let's slow WAY down and do it together. Listen again:
Same one again — no rush. Here's a trick to remember it:
Take a breath. We'll get this one. Tiny hint:
Lesson DONE! 🌟 {name}, you earned every bit of that gold.
And... finished! Feel how that got easier near the end? That's you learning in real time.
We did it! High-five. (I have little starfruit hands but I mean it.)
Complete! The tree grew a little taller today. 🌱
That's a wrap! You knew zero of those words this morning. Wild.
PERFECT lesson — no misses! Tuyệt vời! I'm framing this moment.
Halfway! The hard part's behind us.
We're at the top of the hill — easy from here.
Look, halfway already. Time flies when you're brilliant.
Three in a row! We're cooking. 🔥
FIVE straight! Giỏi quá! Okay now I'm hyped.
TEN. In. A. ROW. Who ARE you?? Incredible.
Our first real words! Greetings and names — exactly what you'd say walking into a room in Vietnam. Let's make a first impression.
Time to be polite. Vietnamese has special words just for being nice, and people NOTICE when you use them. Free charm points.
Café time! ☕ My favorite. We're going to order drinks like we belong here.
Food and prices — the two things you'll use most, honestly. Let's not overpay, okay?
The market! It's loud, it's fun, and we're going to bargain a little. Confidence is the trick.
Numbers, leveled up. Big ones now. Don't panic — there's a pattern, and patterns are my thing.
Getting around! Grab, taxis, motorbikes, directions. Let's make sure we never get lost.
Everyday life stuff — the words you'd actually use every single day. The quiet useful ones.
Talking with people! Making friends, small talk. This is where Vietnamese starts to feel real.
The Vietnamese alphabet looks almost like English... and then it has extra letters wearing little hats. Let's meet them.
Vowels first. These are the sounds everything else sits on top of. Open your ears!
Now the special vowels — ơ, ư, ê, ô. English doesn't have these, so they feel weird at first. That's normal!
Consonants time. Most are easy. A couple are sneaky. I'll warn you about the sneaky ones.
Ending sounds matter a LOT in Vietnamese. A different ending = a different word. Let's get them crisp.
Two vowels holding hands! When they team up, they make a brand new sound. Cute, honestly.
THE BIG ONE. Tones. Today just two: a flat one and a falling one. Hear the difference and you're already winning.
Adding the rising tone — it goes UP, like a question your voice asks. Listen for the lift.
Now the dipping tone — it dives down then climbs back. It's the dramatic one. I love it.
Hỏi vs ngã — okay these two are TWINS and even I mix them up. We'll figure them out together.
All six tones at once. This felt impossible to me a week ago and now look at me. You're gonna get it.
Your turn to SAY them. Be brave, be loud, be a little silly. Nobody's judging — I'm a fruit.
Let's match each little mark to its sound. Once you can read the marks, you can read the tones. Superpower unlocked.
Checkpoint! Show me your ears are ready. Get through this and Unit 1 opens up. I believe in you.
Hi! I'm Bé Khế — a little starfruit who's learning Vietnamese, same as you. Want to learn it together?
Oh, a new friend! I'm Bé Khế. I'm a star, technically. Cut a starfruit and — ta-da — star. Anyway, let's learn Vietnamese!
Before anything — listen to these two. Tell me: same word, or different?
DIFFERENT! Same letters, but the TONE changed the whole meaning. Vietnamese has six of these. Wild, right?
Here's the secret: once your ears can hear the six tones, the rest gets WAY easier. So that's where we start. Tới luôn — let's go!
This is our map! We start at the very bottom and climb. Tap the glowing one — that's our first stop.
First up: Foundations. We learn to HEAR Vietnamese before we speak it. It's the most important part, so we do it first.
See these? They're your tries. Run out and we take a little break — no big deal, they come back.
That's everything! Okay okay okay — I'm excited. Let's actually start.
